item.title: Maynilad volunteers collect 2.26 tons of waste in Manila Bay coastal cleanup
item.dc:creator: Danica Pagarigan
item.description: West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. The volunteers conducted cleanup activities at SM by the Bay; Island B in Barangay Maliksi, Bacoor, Cavite; the Las Piñas-Parañaque Wetlands […]
item.content:encoded:
West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) mobilized 277 volunteers who collected approximately 2.26 tons of waste, equivalent to 327 sacks, from six Manila Bay sites during this year’s International Coastal Cleanup (ICC).

The volunteers conducted cleanup activities at SM by the Bay; Island B in Barangay Maliksi, Bacoor, Cavite; the Las Piñas-Parañaque Wetlands Park; the Coastal Dike in Barangay Bagumbayan North, Navotas; Manila Ocean Park area; and BASECO.

Maynilad also provided drinking water stations at 10 ICC sites around Manila Bay, including the six locations where its volunteers participated in cleanup activities. A hand-washing station was also set up at SM by the Bay.

“Coastal cleanup activities help remove waste that has already reached our waterways, but prevention remains critical. Proper waste disposal in our homes and communities helps keep trash from entering drains, esteros and rivers and eventually reaching Manila Bay,” said Atty. Roel S. Espiritu, Maynilad Chief Sustainability Officer.

Maynilad conducts river, estero and coastal cleanup activities throughout the year as part of its environmental programs. The company also works with communities and partner organizations to help protect waterways within the West Zone and areas surrounding Laguna Lake, one of Maynilad’s raw water sources.

The company’s broader water resource protection initiatives include watershed rehabilitation under its Plant for Life program, which involves the planting and long-term maintenance of indigenous trees in priority watersheds.

The International Coastal Cleanup is an annual global volunteer effort held every September to collect and document waste found along coastlines and waterways.

PHOTO CAPTION: REMOVING WASTE FROM MANILA BAY. Maynilad volunteers retrieve plastic and other debris during this year’s International Coastal Cleanup. A total of 277 volunteers collected 327 sacks, or approximately 2.26 tons, of waste from six cleanup sites around Manila Bay. Maynilad also provided drinking water stations in support of cleanup activities at four more locations.

item.title: Maynilad completes renewable energy roadmap, targets 35% renewable electricity by 2037
item.dc:creator: Danica Pagarigan
item.description: West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) has completed its Renewable Energy Transition Plan, setting out a long-term roadmap to increase the share of renewable energy in the company’s total electricity consumption to 35% by 2037 under its Climate Neutrality Plan. As the first major initiative under the roadmap, Maynilad will increase the renewable […]
item.content:encoded:
West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) has completed its Renewable Energy Transition Plan, setting out a long-term roadmap to increase the share of renewable energy in the company’s total electricity consumption to 35% by 2037 under its Climate Neutrality Plan.

As the first major initiative under the roadmap, Maynilad will increase the renewable energy component of electricity supplied under its contract with MPower, Meralco’s local retail electricity supplier, from 10% to 20% beginning next year. The increase is expected to reduce the company’s carbon emissions by approximately 8,500 metric tons annually.

The Renewable Energy Transition Plan outlines a combination of renewable electricity procurement, on-site solar generation, and energy efficiency initiatives designed to reduce carbon emissions, strengthen energy security, and support the long-term resilience of Maynilad’s water and wastewater operations.

Among the initiatives identified under the roadmap is the installation of new rooftop solar photovoltaic systems at 20 company facilities, including water treatment plants, pumping stations, reservoirs, wastewater treatment plants, and sewage pumping facilities. These will complement Maynilad’s existing solar facilities at the La Mesa Compound and further expand the company’s use of renewable energy.

“The completion of this roadmap marks a major milestone in our sustainability journey. By steadily increasing our use of renewable energy and investing in cleaner technologies, we are reducing our carbon footprint while strengthening the long-term resilience of our operations,” said Maynilad Chief Sustainability Officer Atty. Roel S. Espiritu. The Renewable Energy Transition Plan was developed following an assessment of Maynilad’s energy consumption and carbon emissions, supported by renewable energy feasibility studies and implementation planning. It will guide the company’s renewable electricity procurement and on-site generation projects as it works toward sourcing 35% of its total electricity requirements from renewable energy by 2037.

PHOTO CAPTION: MAYNILAD MAPS SHIFT TO CLEANER ENERGY. Solar photovoltaic (PV) panels at Maynilad’s La Mesa facilities form part of the company’s renewable energy program. Under its newly completed Renewable Energy Transition Plan, Maynilad aims to source 35% of its total electricity requirements from renewable energy by 2037 through expanded renewable electricity procurement, new rooftop solar installations, and energy efficiency initiatives.

item.title: Notice to Maynilad Customers: Foreign Currency Differential Adjustment (FCDA) Effective October 1, 2026

[…]
item.content:encoded:
The Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS), by virtue of Board Resolution No. 2026-119-RO, dated 27 August 2026, as recommended by the MWSS Regulatory Office (RO) in RO Resolution No. 2026-14-CA dated 13 August 2026, granted Maynilad a Foreign Currency Differential Adjustment (FCDA) equivalent to negative 0.02% of the Average Basic Charge of P52.86/cu. m. or an average rebate of P0.01/cu.m. This adjustment will be effective fifteen (15) days after publication or on 01 October 2026. Our Low-Income Lifeline customers consuming 20 cu.m. and below, will be exempt from the adjustment.

FCDA is a tariff mechanism granted to Maynilad to recover or compensate for fluctuations, as the case may be, in the foreign exchange rates arising from Maynilad’s payment of foreign currency-denominated (i) Concession Fees to MWSS, and (ii) loans that Maynilad obtained for its service improvement projects. The FCDA mechanism is based on the principle of “no over or under recovery”.

Maynilad operates the largest water concession by population served within a single concession area in the Philippines. It is a concessionaire of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) for the West Zone of the Greater Manila Area, which is composed of the cities of Manila (certain portions), Quezon City (certain portions), Makati (west of South Super Highway), Caloocan, Pasay, Parañaque, Las Piñas, Muntinlupa, Valenzuela, Navotas and Malabon, all in Metro Manila; the cities of Cavite, Bacoor and Imus, and the municipalities of Kawit, Noveleta and Rosario, all in Cavite Province. Maynilad has 10 Business Area offices across the West Zone that serve its customers

item.content:encoded:
West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) is offering septic tank cleaning services to its residential and semi-business customers this September in select parts of Caloocan, Las Piñas, Manila, Muntinlupa, Parañaque, Pasay, Quezon City, Valenzuela, and Cavite Province at no extra cost.

Maynilad’s sanitation program is one of the company’s efforts to lessen pollution loading into Metro Manila’s river systems. “We ask our customers to avail of this service, as it will help to protect community health and the environment,” said Engr. Zmel Grabillo, Maynilad’s Head of Wastewater Management.

Customers residing in Barangay 80, 89, 138, 139,142 to 146, 148, 149, 151, 160, and 162 in Caloocan; Brgy. Almanza I, Manuyo II, Pamplona 1, Pamplona III, Pillar Village, Pulang Lupa I, Pulang Lupa II, Talon I, and Talon II in Las Piñas; Brgy. Port Area, Quiapo, San Miguel, San Nicolas, Sta. Cruz, and Sta. Mesa in Manila; Brgy. Don Carlos, Maricaban, Pildera 1, San Rafael, and San Roque in Pasay; Brgy. Cupang in Muntinlupa; Brgy. Don Galo, San Martin de Porres, Sun Valley, and Tambo in Parañaque; Brgy. Commonwealth, Nagkaisang Nayon, Paltok, Payatas, Salvacion, San Antonio, San Bartolome, San Isidro, Sta. Lucia, Sta. Monica, and Sto. Niño in Quezon City; and Brgy. Dalandanan, Malinta, Maysan, Parada, Poblacion, and Polo in Valenzuela may avail of Maynilad’s desludging service.

Moreover, some Maynilad customers in Cavite Province, particularly Brgy. Aniban II, Habay I, Kaingin, Ligas II, Ligas III, Mabolo II, Mabolo III, Maliksi II, Maliksi III, Mambog II to Mambog IV, Malino III, Real I, Real II, Salinas I, San Nicolas III, and Sineguelasan in Bacoor City; Brgy. Anabu I-C, Bayan Luma II, Malagasang II-B, Malagasang II-D, Malagasang II-F, Tanzang Luma I to Tanzang Luma VI Toclong I-A, and Toclong I-B in Imus City may avail of the company’s septic tank cleaning services at no extra cost. Septic tank cleaning service normally costs around Php 4,700 per truck.

Maynilad customers interested in availing of the company’s septic tank cleaning service may call the Maynilad Hotline 1626 to determine the requirements and procedures. Additional information is also available in the company’s website, www.mayniladwater.com.ph, and social media accounts (X: @maynilad, Facebook: /MayniladWater).

Maynilad operates the largest water concession by population served within a single concession area in the Philippines. It is a concessionaire of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) for the West Zone of the Greater Manila Area, which is composed of the cities of Manila (certain portions), Quezon City (certain portions), Makati (west of South Super Highway), Caloocan, Pasay, Parañaque, Las Piñas, Muntinlupa, Valenzuela, Navotas and Malabon, all in Metro Manila; the cities of Cavite, Bacoor and Imus, and the municipalities of Kawit, Noveleta and Rosario, all in Cavite Province.

item.title: Maynilad communication programs win five Philippine Quill Awards
item.dc:creator: Danica Pagarigan
item.description: West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) received five awards at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards—three Awards of Excellence and two Awards of Merit—for communication programs supporting water loss reduction, crisis response, public engagement, and the company’s entry into the capital markets. Three Maynilad programs received Awards of Excellence. “Grand Walk-the-Line: Mobilizing Enterprise-Wide Ownership […]
item.content:encoded:
West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services, Inc. (Maynilad) received five awards at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards—three Awards of Excellence and two Awards of Merit—for communication programs supporting water loss reduction, crisis response, public engagement, and the company’s entry into the capital markets.

Three Maynilad programs received Awards of Excellence.

“Grand Walk-the-Line: Mobilizing Enterprise-Wide Ownership for NRW Reduction” was recognized for engaging employees across the organization in Maynilad’s efforts to reduce non-revenue water (NRW), or water that is produced but does not generate revenue because of physical and commercial losses.

“Communicating Through Disruption: Managing the Pritil Leak Repair Incident” received an Award of Excellence under Issues Management and Crisis Communication for the company’s coordinated communications during a major service disruption that required customers to be kept informed amid limited lead time and evolving operational conditions.

Also receiving an Award of Excellence was “Leak Warriors 2025: Turning Citizens into Guardians of Clean Water,” a social media campaign developed with ID8 Inc. that encouraged customers and communities to help report visible leaks. During the campaign period, reported leaks increased by 142% year-on-year.

Maynilad also received two Awards of Merit for communication initiatives supporting its initial public offering (IPO).

“The Maynilad IPO: Building Confidence in the Capital Markets” was recognized under Financial Communication and Investor Relations for communicating the company’s business and long-term growth story to investors ahead of its ₱34.3-billion offering.

Meanwhile, “Shaping the IPO Narrative: Media Relations for Maynilad’s Public Market Debut” received an Award of Merit under Media Relations for helping build understanding of Maynilad’s transition to the public markets.

“These programs addressed very different communication challenges. What ties them together is the need to understand what each audience needs to know and how communication can help them act on that information. These recognitions reinforce our commitment to communication that is clear, timely, responsive, and purposeful,” said Marie Antonette H. de Ocampo, Maynilad Vice President and Head of Corporate Affairs & Communication.

The Philippine Quill Awards, organized by the International Association of Business Communicators (IABC) Philippines, recognize excellence in business communication.

PHOTO CAPTION: Maynilad senior executives and members of the teams behind the company’s winning communication programs receive three Awards of Excellence and two Awards of Merit at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards. The recognized initiatives covered water loss reduction, crisis communication, public engagement, and the company’s entry into the capital markets.
